correctness.rationale: The even-weight shore subspace has one-dimensional orthogonal complement spanned by the all-ones vector. A support loses linear rank exactly when it has a nonempty even-degree subgraph or an all-odd-degree subgraph. The former forces a cycle, the latter exists in a forest exactly when every component has even order. This proves the general claim including isolated vertices. The dimension proof uses the maximal spanning forest, and the online equality uses binary linear-code size. Cayley tree counts and the labeled exponential formula yield the coefficientwise polynomial; standard matroid shellability yields the integral wedge with top Betti equal to the signed face sum. Separate finite Python trace and C++ rank implementations check all edge supports through 6 vertices; an independent labeled-component recurrence checks the polynomial through 10 vertices; direct mod-two boundary ranks check n=4 and 6.

value.rationale: The parity restriction on graph shores is intrinsic to even-cut codes and induces a sharp graph-wide VC/Littlestone rank drop while preserving the binary linear-code structure. The all-graph forest/odd-component criterion identifies every support and the complete-graph specialization yields exact coefficients and integral Betti numbers at all orders; the stated finite values 7, 511, 98099, 36215281 require genuine weighted forest counting and are not only renamings of VC dimension. These supply a concrete benchmark for parity-sensitive matroid complexes.
